International News · 16 Sources · 4 Regions

Daily Brief

The collapse of COP31 climate talks in Antalya dominated headlines Monday, with the EU and Pacific island nations rejecting a final text that omitted any reference to fossil fuels [BBC], [The Economist], [Globe and Mail]. UN Secretary-General António Guterres blamed 'powerful fossil fuel interests' for the failure, the worst breakdown since Copenhagen in 2009. Meanwhile, Ukraine expanded its long-range strike capabilities dramatically, sinking the Russian corvette Merkury in Libya's Benghazi port using naval drones deployed 2,400km from the front line [The Guardian], [Al Jazeera]. The Kremlin warned of 'painful consequences' as both Libyan governments condemned the strikes. In a remarkable corporate reversal, Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO just days after the board ruled out his return, with President Trump claiming he personally intervened with the company [France 24], [Financial Times]. Democratic Senator Chuck Schumer vowed investigations into potential wrongdoing. Across Europe, Belgium ground to a halt as a national strike against austerity measures cancelled over 400 flights and shut down public transport [BBC], affecting more than 50,000 passengers as coalition budget negotiations continue.

01 Climate

COP31 Climate Talks Collapse as EU Rejects Fossil Fuel-Free Final Text

  • UN climate conference in Antalya, Turkey ended Sunday without agreement after becoming the longest COP in history, extending two days past deadline
  • Final draft text contained no mention of fossil fuels or transition away from them, prompting formal objections from EU, Pacific island nations, and Panama
  • UN Secretary-General António Guterres blamed 'powerful fossil fuel interests' for blocking progress, comparing tactics to 'Big Tobacco's playbook'
  • First major COP failure since Copenhagen in 2009; Australian PM Albanese attributed collapse to 'difficult geopolitical times'

Ukraine Sinks Russian Warship in Libya Using Long-Range Naval Drones

  • Ukrainian forces deployed seven domestically-made naval drones to sink the corvette Merkury at Benghazi naval base, 2,400km from Ukraine's front line
  • A second Russian cargo ship, MV Angara, was also struck; Ukraine claims it was transporting weapons
  • Both Libyan governments condemned the attack; Kremlin warned of 'escalation of tensions' and 'painful consequences'
  • Operation marks significant expansion of Ukraine's long-range strike capability beyond the Black Sea

Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO After Trump Claims Direct Intervention

  • Nvidia board unanimously voted to reinstate co-founder Jensen Huang as CEO, effective immediately, reversing position from days earlier
  • Trump told CNBC he directly intervened with Nvidia's board to bring Huang back after his resignation amid affair revelations including alleged Chinese spy
  • Democratic Senate leader Chuck Schumer vowed full investigation into potential wrongdoing, accusing Trump of prioritizing financial interests over national security
  • Nvidia shares surged approximately 30-33%, driving Nasdaq up 7% and S&P up 4.3%
